study_identification_part.si4_title: Lifespan Normative Modeling of Brain Microstructure

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To construct large-scale normative models of white matter microstructure across the lifespan using diffusion MRI data from 19 international datasets, derive centile trajectories by age and sex, and demonstrate clinical utility through anomaly detection in mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.

rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We included the following public datasets with various age ranges to cover the lifespan: the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD), the Amsterdam Open MRI Collection (AOMIC), the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (CAMCAN), the Cuban Human Brain Mapping Project (CHBMP), the Chinese Human Connectome Project (CHCP), the Human Connectome Project Aging & Development (HCP_A & HCP_D), the Human Connectome Project Young Adult (HCP_YA), the DTI component of the NIH MRI Study of Normal Brain Development (PedsDTI), the Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition, and Genetics data repository (PING), the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort (PNC), the Queensland Twin Adolescent Brain (QTAB), the Queensland Twin Imaging dataset (QTIM), the Southwest University Longitudinal Imaging Multimodal (SLIM) study, and the UK BioBank (UKBB). Several clinical datasets were also included in the analyses: the third phase of the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI3), the third release of the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS3), the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI), and the Healthy Brain Network (HBN). Importantly, only the healthy controls (HC) of the latter four datasets were added to the pool of training data to build the normative models, yielding a total of 19 public datasets.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: DiPy (tensor fitting); FSL (dtifit; flirt for linear registration); ANTs (diffeomorphic nonlinear registration); 3DMI (for QTIM nonlinear registration); ENIGMA-DTI protocol (for ROI extraction); JHU-WM atlas; HCP, ABCD, and AOMIC provided preprocessed dMRI; PedsDTI and UKBB provided precomputed DTI maps
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The preprocessing pipeline is described in detail, including software used for tensor fitting, registration, and ROI extraction. Dataset-specific preprocessing is noted.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: DTI maps (FA, MD, RD and AD) were computed with DiPy's tensor fitting function for the following datasets: AOMIC, CAMCAN, CHBMP, CHCP, HCP_A, HCP_D, HCP_YA, NIMHANS, PNC, QTAB and UCLA. FSL's dtifit was used to fit the diffusion tensor for ABCD, ADNI3, HBN, OASIS3, PING, PPMI, QTIM, SLIM. All subjects' FA maps were linearly registered with FSL's flirt and nonlinearly registered to the ENIGMA-FA template with ANTs' diffeomorphic non-linear registration algorithm. For QTIM, nonlinear registration was performed using the 3DMI algorithm. Mean DTI metrics were extracted from 21 bilateral regions of interest (regions) from the Johns Hopkins University WM atlas (JHU-WM) using the ENIGMA-DTI protocol.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Manual QC for ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, CAMCAN, HBN assessed head movement, FOV artifacts, dMRI acquisition artifacts, and preprocessing errors. Automated QC using isolation forests (Scikit-learn) applied to remaining datasets; run separately on each ROI for each DTI metric; subjects flagged as outliers in at least two DTI metrics were removed. Final training sample: 54,583 subjects after QC.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: ADNI3, OASIS3, PPMI, CAMCAN and HBN were manually checked for head movement, FOV (field of view) related artifacts and other dMRI acquisition artifacts and preprocessing errors caused by poorly tuned software tools. For all other datasets used for training, outliers were detected with an anomaly detection algorithm called isolation forests implemented in Scikit-learn... isolation forests were run on each ROI for each DTI metric, separately, to identify a subset of 'outlier subjects' for each DTI metric. Subsequently, outlier subjects that were duplicated in at least two DTI metrics were removed from the sample. Aggregating the subjects left after this procedure plus the subjects from the datasets that were manually checked, a total of 54,583 subjects remained for training.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: HBR with partial pooling strategy: dMRI acquisition protocol used as batch effect (37 distinct protocols identified across 19 datasets, detailed in Table S1); sex modeled as second grouping variable (random effect) in HBR; age modeled with cubic b-spline basis expansion (5 evenly spaced knots) as fixed independent variable. HBR estimates separate parameters for μ (mean) and σ (noise standard deviation) for each batch via hyperpriors, preventing overfitting on small batches. Z-score harmonization occurs by adjusting for additive and multiplicative batch effects. ComBat harmonization explicitly avoided to preserve biological variance correlated with age and site.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: We identified 37 dMRI acquisition protocols across the 19 datasets (see Table S1)... we used the dMRI protocol as the batch effect when training the normative model with HBR. HBR models these site-dependent parameters in a hyperprior, and the model hyperparameters are adapted to incoming data from each site. Subsequently, we ran an HBR model for each DTI metric across all regions that included sex as a second grouping variable in the HBR setting, and age as a fixed independent variable... we modeled the non-linear effect of age with a cubic b-spline basis set expansion with five evenly spaced knots... an assumption in HBR is that (and σ) across different batches come from the same joint prior distribution that functions as a regularizer and prevents overfitting on small batches. HBR is described as a partial pooling strategy in the multi-site scenario... The harmonization of Z-scores happens at this stage where the Z-scores are adjusted for additive and multiplicative batch effects using the estimated μ and σ for each batch. In fact, the model does not yield a set of 'harmonized' data, i.e., with the batch variability removed. Instead, it preserves the sources of biological variability that may correlate with the batch effects. When removing the site effect with harmonization methods such as ComBat some of the biological variance correlated with age and site may be inadvertently removed.

Z-scores were also calculated for the Alzheimer's dementia and MCI cases from ADNI3 and OASIS3. We calculated the probabilities of abnormality P(z), i.e., the abnormality scores, from the Z-scores for both controls (20% sample split) and clinical samples (dementia and MCI) using the following formula... ROI-wise areas under the ROC curves (AUCs) were calculated to determine the classification accuracy of the computed deviations... For each clinical group, i.e., dementia and MCI, we summarized the individual deviations within each group by first separating them into positive and negative deviations, counting how many subjects had an extreme deviation (defined as Z>2 for positive deviations, Z<-2 for negative deviations) at a given ROI, and then dividing by the group size.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: ROI-wise AUCs computed for classifying patients (MCI or dementia) versus healthy controls across 10 experimental repetitions. Permutation tests (1,000 random samples) used to derive p-values for each DTI metric per ROI. False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction applied separately for each DTI metric across regions. Regions showing significance in at least 9 out of 10 iterations were retained. Individual deviations summarized by separating into positive/negative extreme deviations (|Z|>2), counting subjects with extreme deviations per ROI, and computing percentage of clinical group. Results reported as AUC values and percentage of subjects with extreme deviations per region.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Large-scale HBR normative models of white matter microstructure (N=54,583; age 4-91 years) successfully characterize lifespan trajectories with inverted U-shaped curves for FA and U-shaped for diffusivities, detect clinically meaningful deviations in MCI, dementia, and 22q11.2 deletion syndrome, and demonstrate robust transferability through model adaptation to independent external datasets.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative models were fitted to FA, MD, AD, and RD across 22 white matter regions, revealing characteristic lifespan patterns: FA peaked between 16-39 years across regions (Global-WM at 29 years), while diffusivities showed U-shaped trajectories with minima at 30-53 years. Model diagnostics showed good fit (median SMSE <0.67, MSLL <-0.24) with AD showing best performance. Anomaly detection in dementia achieved highest AUCs in CGH (RD: 0.74, MD: 0.70, FA: 0.65) and BCC (AD: 0.67). MCI showed lower but significant AUCs (0.55-0.67), with best performance in SCC (MD: 0.60), BCC (AD: 0.67), and FX (FA/MD: 0.58/0.59). Extreme deviations (|Z|>2) were predominantly positive for diffusivities and negative for FA: dementia showed 37% positive RD deviations in CGH and 25% in SCC; MCI showed 17% positive RD deviations in SCC and 11% in CGH. Model adaptation to NIMHANS (India) successfully detected MCI/dementia patterns, while adaptation to UCLA identified 22qDel effects showing negative MD/AD deviations in corona radiata regions. Retrogenesis analysis found limited support: MD showed evidence for 'last-in first-out' hypothesis (Rho=0.47, p=0.03) but no evidence for 'gain-predicts-loss' hypothesis across DTI metrics.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Batch variable defined by dMRI acquisition protocol (37 distinct protocols across 19 datasets, detailed in Table S1). Age modeled with cubic b-splines (5 evenly spaced knots) as fixed effect. Sex modeled as second grouping variable (random effect) in HBR. Models trained with NUTS sampler (No-U-Turn Sampler) on 80% splits (n=43,666). Posterior predictive distribution sampled for inference on test data (20% splits, n=10,917). Model adaptation used PCNtoolkit 'transfer' function to adapt hyperparameters to new sites using 50% of local healthy controls. Trained models to be made publicly available at PCNPortal (https://pcnportal.dccn.nl/).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: ENIGMA-DTI protocol not optimized for very early childhood (3-5 years), requiring specialized infant pipelines for this age range. Potential CSF partial volume contamination in regions near ventricles (fornix, tapetum) may affect distributional properties (elevated kurtosis, skewness). Single-shell DTI acquisition limits microstructural specificity as FA reflects composite of axonal density, myelination, orientation dispersion, crossing fibers, and free-water. Advanced multi-compartmental models (Standard Model Imaging, NODDI) requiring multi-shell data would provide more specific microstructural information but are not yet widely available clinically. Some regions (fornix, cingulum, splenium) showed non-monotonic 'double peak' trajectories around age 50-60, potentially reflecting free-water effects from atrophy. More sophisticated distributional models (warping, SHASH, VAEs) may better capture non-Gaussian distributions in some regions.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is the first large-scale lifespan normative model for white matter microstructure based on diffusion MRI. Training data aggregated from 19 international datasets spanning 37 distinct dMRI acquisition protocols. Study covers nearly complete lifespan (4-91 years) with N=54,583 after QC. Models generated separately for males and females as sex-specific trajectories. Clinical applications demonstrated in both neurodevelopmental (22qDel, age ~14 years) and neurodegenerative (MCI/dementia, age 60s-70s) conditions. Paper includes extensive supplementary analyses: ROI-specific trajectories (Figures S1-S4), diagnostic metrics per ROI (Figures S5-S8), retrogenesis hypothesis testing (Figures S9-S16), and detailed extreme deviation tables (Tables S2-S11). Preprocessing varied by dataset: three studies (HCP_YA, ABCD, AOMIC) provided preprocessed dMRI; two (PedsDTI, UKBB) provided precomputed DTI maps; remaining datasets preprocessed in-house. All data registered to ENIGMA-FA template using FSL/ANTs pipeline. Future directions suggested include multi-shell acquisitions, advanced microstructural models, tractometry approaches, and more sophisticated distributional models (warping, SHASH, VAEs).
